correctness.rationale: On the Bernoulli Koopman space, coordinate sign functions give a reducing bilateral shift, hence full unit-circle spectral support. Direct integral over U transfers the infinite-operator resolvent to sup_{|eta|=r}||(M-eta I)^-1||. Exact upper-bidiagonal inverse entries have unique nonzero path; |d_i-eta|>=|d_i-r| and row/column signs factor at real r, so entrywise majorization yields equality at eta=r for operator 2-norm. For m=2, the smaller singular value on [a,b] maximizes at midpoint, with eps*=(sqrt((b-a)^2+gamma^2)-gamma)/2; monotonicity outside spectral circles and strict < for open pseudospectrum give two components at equality and merger only for epsilon>eps*. Spectrum itself is union of diagonal circles. Proof does not rely on the numerical diagnostic.
